text:
devon: hey @anya @liam — I pushed the PR that wires up the new VPC peering + auth changes for on-prem customers, can you do a quick security/privacy review? PR: https://git.internal/redwood/redwood-platform/pull/4822 :eyes:

anya: thanks — pinging. quick Q: does this PR add any new plaintext secrets into env or config files? skim looks like kms integration but want to be sure. :mag:

devon: no plaintext secrets in the repo. added a tiny terraform module that references a customer KMS key id and updates the vpn route. snippet:```hcl
resource "aws_kms_key" "customer_key" {
  description = var.kms_desc
  policy      = var.kms_policy
}
```
but the module expects `var.kms_key_id` passed from infra pipeline. secrets remain in vault/KMS.

liam: fwiw, the Dedicated deployment templates change the `private_ip_range` and add VPC peering. On-prem package bundles a connector binary that will use mTLS certs stored in the customer's vault. No hardcoded creds.

anya: ok good. couple follow-ups: 1) add a note in the PR description describing where keys live and who has access (key admins). 2) confirm audit logging for KMS usage is enabled for new keys. 3) double-check service account scopes for the connector — least privilege?

devon: will update PR desc and add `audit_logging = true` to the terraform. for SA scopes I limited to `compute.networkAdmin` + `kms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` per the infra guide.

june: timeline? customer is on a short runway, they want enablement by EOW. is a security sign-off blocking merge?

anya: I can do a final pass today if devon adds the desc + logging flag. after that I need one more approval from infra (liam) and a quick ops checklist run.

liam: I can review in the next 2 hours. one heads-up: when we enable peering we must update the routing table entries in staging first — I left a checklist comment in the PR. also run `make infra-plan` and attach plan output.

infra-bot: CI / terraform-plan failed on the last run: 
```
Error: Insufficient permissions to read KMS key
  on modules/customer_kms/main.tf line 12, in data "aws_kms_key" "existing":
  12: data "aws_kms_key" "existing" {
```

devon: thanks infra-bot, I see. that's because the pipeline role in staging didn't have kms:DescribeKey. adding that to the role policy now, will re-run.

anya: once the pipeline role fix is in, please add a short entry in the security-runbook: "new-customer-kms-keys" — list who to contact and which logs to check (CloudTrail, KMS logs). link to runbook in PR.

devon: will do. plan: 1) update PR desc + add runbook link, 2) flip `audit_logging = true`, 3) update pipeline role, re-run plan, 4) request final from @liam and @anya. aiming to merge today.

june: perfect — keep me posted. if you need me to push the enablement date back for the customer, say the word. :white_check_mark:

anya: quick reminder: for Private/on-prem customers we need to ensure customer-provided certs are stored only in their vault and never echoed in logs. add a `sensitive = true` on any TF output that returns cert IDs.

devon: good catch, will add `sensitive = true`. thanks all.

sre-bot: noted: escalate to oncall if any certs appear in logs. automated alert rule exists: `log_contains(cert.pem)` -> pager.

liam: LGTM pending the updates. I'll approve after infra-plan passes.

devon: thanks everyone — will push updates in ~30m and ping here when done. :rocket:
